<!--
Task:   Descriptive time series figures (Fig. 2, daily series, histograms).
Input:  data/Austria-Panel-Daily-de_en.csv
        data/newsguard/shared_domains.csv (not released; the domain plot is skipped without it)
Output: output/figures/desc_prop_plot.pdf, desc_plot.pdf, desc_daily.pdf, trustworthiness_daily.pdf,
        emotions_daily.pdf, vars_histograms.pdf, domains_plot.pdf
Run:    As R Markdown or in terminal as Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("2b-plot_time_series.Rmd")'   # variants: LANG, DISGUST in the parameters chunk
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(readr)
library(scales)
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(patchwork) # arrange grids
library(forecast) # ARIMA
library(tseries)
library(TSA)
library(vars) # VAR modeling
library(lmtest)
library(tsoutliers) #tsoutliers
library(urca)  # ca.jo, ur.df, finland
library(tsDyn) # VECM

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(scipen=999)
```

```{r parameters}
src <- "../../data"
dst <- "../../output"
dir.create(file.path(dst, "figures"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
LANG <- "de_en"   # de_en (main), de, all
DISGUST <- FALSE  # FALSE (main), TRUE (robustness: + disgust; validation failed)
tag  <- paste0(if (LANG == "de_en") "" else paste0("_", LANG), if (DISGUST) "_disgust" else "")
```

```{r custom plots}

custom_plot <- function() {
  theme_classic() +  
    theme(
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 12),
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 11),
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 11),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 11)
    )
}

knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3)

```

# Exploration of time series data

```{r}
daily_summary <- read.csv(file.path(src, paste0("Austria-Panel-Daily-", LANG, ".csv")))
head(daily_summary, 2)
```

```{r}
daily_summary$day <- as.Date(daily_summary$day, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
summary(daily_summary)
```

```{r}
daily_summary <- daily_summary %>% arrange(day)
head(daily_summary, 5)
```

```{r}
start_date <- min(daily_summary$day)
start_year <- year(start_date)
start_day  <- yday(start_date)  # day of year for start
```

```{r}
# create proportions
daily_summary <- daily_summary %>%
  mutate(
    prop_news = (count_ng_domains / tweet_count) * 100,
    prop_misinfo = ((count_caution + count_max_caution) / tweet_count) * 100,
    prop_anger = (count_anger_065 / n_scored) * 100,
    prop_fear = (count_fear_065 / n_scored) * 100,
    prop_disgust = (count_disgust_065 / n_scored) * 100,
    prop_right = (count_right / tweet_count) * 100,
    prop_left = (count_left / tweet_count)*100
  )

proportions <- c("prop_news", "prop_misinfo", "prop_anger", "prop_fear",
                 if (DISGUST) "prop_disgust", "prop_right", "prop_left")
hist_labels <- c(prop_news = "News sharing (%)", prop_misinfo = "Untrustworthy news (%)",
                 prop_anger = "Anger (%)", prop_fear = "Fear (%)", prop_disgust = "Disgust (%)",
                 prop_right = "Right-leaning news (%)", prop_left = "Left-leaning news (%)")
summary(daily_summary[, proportions])

# untrustworthy news for the manuscript: daily share of all tweets and of all
# news links (mean, SD, max), and pooled shares over the whole period
daily_summary %>%
  mutate(of_tweets = (count_caution + count_max_caution) / tweet_count * 100,
         of_news   = (count_caution + count_max_caution) / count_ng_domains * 100) %>%
  summarise(across(c(of_tweets, of_news), list(mean = mean, sd = sd, max = max))) %>%
  round(3)
with(daily_summary, round(c(
  pooled_of_tweets = sum(count_caution + count_max_caution) / sum(tweet_count) * 100,
  pooled_of_news   = sum(count_caution + count_max_caution) / sum(count_ng_domains) * 100), 3))
```

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=6}
pdf(file.path(dst, paste0("figures/vars_histograms", tag, ".pdf")), width = 8, height = 8)
par(mfrow = c(3,3), 
    cex.main = 1.5,    
    cex.lab = 1.3,    
    cex.axis = 1.2) 

for (p in proportions) {
  var_mean <- mean(daily_summary[[p]], na.rm = TRUE)
  
  hist(daily_summary[[p]], 
       main = paste(""),
       xlab = hist_labels[[p]],
       ylab = "",
       col = "lightblue",
       border = "black")
  abline(v = var_mean, col = "red", lwd = 2)
}
dev.off()

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
p_count <- ggplot(daily_summary, aes(x = day, y = tweet_count)) +
  geom_line() +
  custom_plot()+
  labs(tag="a", y="# tweets")+
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))


p_news <- ggplot(daily_summary, aes(x = day, y = count_ng_domains)) +
  geom_line() +
  custom_plot()+
  labs(tag="b", y="# news links")+
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"))

desc_daily <- (p_count / p_news)

ggsave(file.path(dst, "figures/desc_daily.pdf"), 
          desc_daily, 
          width = 9, height = 4.5)
```

## Weekly averages
```{r}
# summarize per week to visualize
daily_summary <- daily_summary%>%
  mutate(
    count_trustworthy = count_exceptions + count_generally_credible + count_high_credibility,
    count_untrustworthy = count_max_caution + count_caution
  )

weekly_summary <- daily_summary %>%
dplyr:::select(day, tweet_count, count_ng_domains, 
               count_trustworthy, count_untrustworthy,
               mean_score, mean_anger, mean_fear, mean_disgust) %>%
  mutate(week = floor_date(day, "week")) %>%  # Create week column
  group_by(week) %>%
  summarise(
    across(c(tweet_count, count_ng_domains, count_trustworthy, count_untrustworthy), sum, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(c(mean_score, mean_anger, mean_fear, mean_disgust), mean, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

```

```{r}
domestic <- "gray42"
global <- "black"

events <- data.frame(
  date = as.Date(c("2019-05-17", 
                   "2020-03-12", 
                   "2020-11-02", 
                   "2021-01-06", 
                   "2021-10-09", 
                   "2022-02-24", 
                   "2022-10-21")),
  event = c("Ibiza scandal",  
            "COVID-19 lockdown",
            "Vienna attack",
            "Capitol storming", 
            "Advertisement scandal",
            "Russian invasion\n of Ukraine",
            "Woman, Life,\nFreedom protests"),
  color = c(domestic, domestic, domestic, global, domestic, global, global),
  linetype = c("dashed", "dashed", "dashed", "dotted", "dashed", "dotted", "dotted")
)

```

```{r}
max_tweets <- max(weekly_summary$tweet_count, na.rm = TRUE)

tweets_plot <- ggplot(data=weekly_summary, 
                      aes(x = week, 
                          y = tweet_count)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data=events, 
             aes(xintercept = date), 
             color = events$color, 
             linetype = events$linetype,
             alpha = 0.9) +
  ggrepel:::geom_text_repel(
                  data=events, 
                  aes(x = date-50, 
                      y = max_tweets * 1.02, 
                      label = event),
                  color = events$color, 
                  size = 2.88,
                  hjust=0, 
                  direction = "y", 
                  nudge_x=0,
                  lineheight=0.7,
                  force=3, 
                  ylim = c(max_tweets * 0.95, 
                           max_tweets * 1.45),  
                  segment.color = "transparent") + 
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +  
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) + 
  labs(tag="a", x = "", y = "# tweets") +
  custom_plot() +
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(t = 50, r = 5, b = 0, l = 5, unit = "pt"),
    plot.tag = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )

news_plot <- ggplot(data = weekly_summary, 
                  aes(x = week, 
                      y = count_ng_domains)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data = events, 
             aes(xintercept = date), 
             color = events$color, 
             linetype = events$linetype,
             alpha = 0.9) +
  labs(
    tag="b",
    x = "",
    y = "# news shared"
  ) +
  custom_plot()+
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))

score_plot <- ggplot(data = weekly_summary, 
                     aes(x = week, y = mean_score)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data = events, 
             aes(xintercept = date), 
             color = events$color, 
             linetype = events$linetype, alpha = 0.9) +
  labs(
    tag="c",
    x = "time in weeks",
    y = "avg.\n trustworthiness"
  ) +
  custom_plot()+
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))

desc_plot <- (tweets_plot / news_plot / score_plot)
```

```{r}
ggsave(file.path(dst, "figures/desc_plot.pdf"), 
          desc_plot, 
          width = 9, height = 6)
```

```{r}
plot_data <- weekly_summary %>%
  mutate(
    prop_untrustworthy = (count_untrustworthy / count_ng_domains) * 100,
    prop_trustworthy = (count_trustworthy / count_ng_domains) * 100
    ) %>%
  dplyr:::select(week, prop_trustworthy, prop_untrustworthy) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(prop_trustworthy, prop_untrustworthy),
    names_to = "type",
    values_to = "proportion",
    names_prefix = "prop_"
  )

prop_plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = week, y = proportion, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 7, alpha=0.8) + 
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("trustworthy" = "#4daf4a", "untrustworthy" = "#984ea3"),
    labels = c("trustworthy", "untrustworthy")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "date",
    y = "trustworthiness\n of news (%)",
    tag="b") +
  custom_plot()+
  theme(
    plot.margin = margin(t = 2, r = 5, b = 5, l = 5, unit = "pt"),
    plot.tag = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = c(0.65, 1.1), 
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.title=element_blank(),
    legend.text=element_text(size=9),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", color = NA), 
    legend.key.size = unit(0.25, "cm") 
  )

desc_prop_plot <- (tweets_plot / prop_plot)
ggsave(file.path(dst, "figures/desc_prop_plot.pdf"), 
          desc_prop_plot, 
          width = 6, height = 3.5)
```



## Domain analysis
The NewsGuard data is proprietary so the below data cannot be shared. 

# Domain ratings
```{r}
HAS_NG <- file.exists(file.path(src, "newsguard/shared_domains.csv"))
if (!HAS_NG) message("newsguard/shared_domains.csv not found (restricted NewsGuard data): skipping domain section.")
```

```{r, eval = HAS_NG}
domain_tweets <- read.csv(file.path(src, "newsguard/shared_domains.csv"), sep=",")
nrow(domain_tweets)
```

```{r, eval = HAS_NG}
domain_tweets <- domain_tweets %>%
  filter(file_month <= "2023-04")
nrow(domain_tweets)
```

```{r, eval = HAS_NG, fig.height=2.5, fig.width=6}
domain_tweets$file_month <- as.Date(paste0(domain_tweets$file_month, "-01"))
domain_agg <- domain_tweets %>%
  group_by(file_month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_untrustworthy = n_distinct(Domain[Score < 60]),
    n_sources = n_distinct(Domain),
    fraction_untrustworthy = (n_untrustworthy / n_sources)*100
  )

domains_plot <- ggplot(domain_agg, aes(x = file_month)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = mean_score, color = "mean")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = 75 + (fraction_untrustworthy / 30)*10, 
                color = "fraction")) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "avg. trustworthiness",
    limits = c(75, 85),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ (. - 75) / 10* 30,
                        name = "domains < 60 (%)",
                        breaks = seq(0,30, by=10))
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("mean" = "black", "fraction" = "gray")) +
  labs(x = "time in months", color = "") +
  custom_plot()

plot(domains_plot)
```

```{r, eval = HAS_NG}
ggsave(file.path(dst, "figures/domains_plot.pdf"), 
          domains_plot, 
          width = 9, height = 3)
```


```{r, eval = HAS_NG}
ggplot(domain_agg, aes(x = file_month,y = n_sources)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "time in months", y= "sources (n)")+
  custom_plot()
```
